The program integrates knowledge from across the biological and physical sciences, including chemistry, biology, physics, and mathematics, to study the environment and find solutions to environmental problems. The curriculum consists of a core of foundation courses, introductory and capstone courses in environmental science, and a wide range of elective courses allowing students to tailor their education to specific interests such as ecology, atmospheric sciences, geosciences, or water resources. Students will learn to integrate knowledge from various scientific disciplines to understand environmental systems, use scientific methods to design studies and analyze results, and apply scientific knowledge to address critical environmental issues.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Sciences
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf

description: Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the processes that control the environment, the impacts of human activities on these processes, and the implications of environmental change for the health and well-being of the planet. The Environmental Sciences major provides a rigorous science-based curriculum that prepares students to address some of the most pressing environmental challenges of our time. Students in the major gain a strong foundation in the physical, biological, and social sciences, and develop the skills needed to analyze and solve environmental problems. The curriculum includes core courses in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics, as well as specialized courses in environmental science, such as atmospheric science, ecology, geology, and soil science. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research and internships, providing hands-on experience in the field.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Sciences
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Environmental Studies major is a unique, additional major that must be paired with another major. This interdisciplinary approach allows students to explore the environment through many different lenses – including history, ethics, economics, ecology, and more – and build the tools to address our world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Because students pair environmental studies with another major, they are able to integrate environmental perspectives into any field of study, from business and engineering to history and the arts. This creates a flexible and diverse learning environment that helps students see the environment from many perspectives and gives them the skills to solve problems in a variety of fields. Through this program, students learn to think across boundaries through coursework in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences; understand the complex relationship between humans and the environment; tackle real-world environmental problems; and gain skills in research, writing, and communication.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies
Program Page url: https://nelson.wisc.edu/undergraduate/environmental-studies-major/

description: Environmental studies is a co-major. It must be taken in conjunction with another undergraduate major. Students may choose any other major offered at UW–Madison. Environmental studies provides a unique opportunity to look at any major through an environmental lens. Environmental studies is a flexible, interdisciplinary major that can be paired with any other major on campus, from biology or community and environmental sociology to history, business, or engineering. Students in environmental studies work to understand the complex interactions between humans and nature. They develop the skills and knowledge to address environmental problems from multiple perspectives—scientific, social, and humanistic. The program's interdisciplinary approach prepares students to be informed citizens and leaders in a wide range of fields. The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies was established in 1970 and renamed in 2002 to honor former Wisconsin governor and U.S. Senator Gaylord Nelson, the founder of Earth Day. The institute serves as a campus-wide hub for interdisciplinary environmental initiatives, and it is a national leader in environmental education and research.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Finance major prepares students for careers in corporate financial management, commercial and investment banking, and investment management. Students develop an understanding of the concepts of valuation, risk-return trade-offs, financial statement analysis, and capital structure. They are also introduced to the analysis and evaluation of investments such as common stocks, fixed income securities, and derivatives. In addition, students study the operations and roles of financial markets and institutions in a global context. The major also provides an understanding of how businesses and individual investors obtain and manage financial resources. Finance students develop their analytical and problem-solving skills using various methodologies and tools including spreadsheets, databases, and financial modeling.
Program name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance, Investment and Banking
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/finance/business-finance-investment-banking-bba/

description: Food science is a multidisciplinary field that applies chemistry, microbiology, engineering, and nutrition to develop new food products and design processes to improve the safety and quality of food. The food science major at UW–Madison is known for its rigorous curriculum, which prepares students for careers in the food industry, government, and academia. Students in the program learn about food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering, and food processing. They also gain hands-on experience in the department's state-of-the-art pilot plants and laboratories. The program is designed to meet the standards set by the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT), ensuring that students receive a high-quality education that is recognized by employers worldwide.
Accreditation status: The Food Science major is approved by the Higher Education Review Board (HERB) of the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT).
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Food Science
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/food-science/food-science-bs/

description: Society's need for forest products and the desire for diverse forest-based services—such as clean water, wildlife habitat, and outdoor recreation—continue to grow. To meet these demands, the forest science major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to manage forest resources sustainably and for the benefit of all. The forest science major is a professional program that emphasizes the economic, social, and environmental aspects of forest management. Students learn to apply the principles of ecology, biology, and the physical sciences to the management of forest ecosystems. Graduates are prepared for careers in forest management, conservation, and research with government agencies, non-profit organizations, and private companies. The forest science major is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).
Accreditation status: The forest science major is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Forest Science
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/forest-wildlife-ecology/forest-science-bs/

description: The French major at UW–Madison allows students to improve their French language skills while exploring the literature, culture, and history of the French-speaking world. In our courses, students develop proficiency in communication and gain an understanding of the diversity of the Francophone world. Beyond the classroom, students may choose to live in the French-speaking wing of the International Learning Community (the French House), participate in the French Club, or attend the weekly French conversation table (the Café Français). Many students also choose to study abroad in a French-speaking country, which is an excellent way to immerse themselves in the language and culture. Students who major in French are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as international business, government, education, law, and the non-profit sector. French is an official language in 29 countries and is one of the official languages of the United Nations, the European Union, and the International Olympic Committee.
Program Page url: https://www.admissions.txst.edu/explore/academics/majors-and-degrees.html

description: The Department of French and Italian offers a wide range of opportunities for the study of French and Italian languages and literatures. These programs are designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the language and culture of France and Francophone countries and of Italy. French is a major language of international culture, being one of the official languages of the United Nations, and is spoken by more than 200 million people on five continents. Students will find that the study of French or Italian is a great goal in itself and a wonderful complement to many other majors in the humanities, social sciences, and sciences. For students interested in international studies, French or Italian is a natural fit. More than half of French majors at UW–Madison are double majors. The Department of French and Italian is committed to providing students with an understanding of French and Italian cultures in a global context. The department offers courses in language, literature, culture, and film, and its programs are designed to meet the needs of students with a variety of goals.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Gender and women's studies is an interdisciplinary field that challenges us to consider how our lives are shaped by gender. Students analyze the impact of gender and its intersection with other social categories—such as race, class, ethnicity, sexuality, and disability—within our legal, economic, and political systems, as well as in our homes, our communities, and our own bodies. Gender and women’s studies courses cover a wide range of topics, including feminist theory, women’s history, LGBTQ+ studies, global feminism, and gender and health. The Gender and Women’s Studies major at UW–Madison is one of the oldest and most respected programs in the country. Our faculty are leading scholars in their fields, and our students are passionate about making a difference in the world. A major in gender and women’s studies provides students with strong critical thinking, writing, and research skills that are highly valued by employers in a variety of fields, including law, medicine, social work, education, and public policy. Our graduates go on to successful careers in a wide range of areas, including non-profit organizations, government agencies, and the private sector.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Women's Studies
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/gender-womens-studies/gender-womens-studies-ba/

description: The Department of Gender and Women's Studies is a vibrant community of students and scholars at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Since its creation in 1975, the department has grown into a world-renowned program that offers students many opportunities to explore how we live our lives as gendered beings in a variety of cultural and historical contexts. Students study how gender and sexuality intersect with other categories of identity, such as race, ethnicity, class, disability, and nationality. Our curriculum prepares students to be leaders in the community, providing them with the necessary tools to navigate an increasingly global world. Gender and women’s studies (GWS) provides students with a high degree of flexibility in choosing their courses while also ensuring that they understand the foundations of the field and its core themes. Students learn to think critically, to work across disciplines, and to approach social problems in a multifaceted way. Many of our students are double majors, combining their interest in GWS with other fields such as nursing, social work, history, biology, sociology, political science, psychology, or world languages. Graduates go on to pursue careers in such areas as law, medicine, public policy, social work, teaching, non-profit management, business, and many others.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Gender and Women's Studies
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Genetics is the study of how traits are inherited and how the information that guides the development and function of an organism is stored and transmitted between generations. Genetics is at the heart of many of the most significant advances in biology today and provides the tools and framework for our modern understanding of all of the life sciences. From new treatments for cancer and rare diseases to new ways to address climate change and increase the global food supply, genetics is at the forefront of innovation. The Genetics and Genomics program offers students a solid foundation in the principles of genetics, while also providing them with the opportunity to explore the latest developments in genomics and the many ways that genetics is being used to address global challenges. Students in the program learn about the molecular basis of inheritance, the structure and function of genomes, the genetic basis of complex traits, and the role of genetics in evolution and development. They also gain experience in the laboratory and develop skills in data analysis and critical thinking.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Genetics and Genomics
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/genetics/genetics-modern-world-certificate/

description: Geography is the study of the earth as the home of humanity. It is a diverse and integrative discipline that bridges the physical and social sciences. Geography is a spatial science that looks at the ways in which physical and human phenomena are distributed over space, why they are there, and how they interact. The geography major at UW–Madison is broad and flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests. The major includes courses in physical geography, human geography, people–environment geography, and cartography and geographic information systems (GIS). Students can choose to focus their studies in one of these areas or take a broad approach that covers multiple areas.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/geography-ba/

description: Geography is the study of the Earth’s systems and the interactions between people and their environments. Geographers investigate the processes that shape the Earth’s surface, the ways that humans use and perceive the landscape, and the patterns of human activity across space and time. Geography is a diverse field that includes both the physical and social sciences, as well as the humanities. The Geography major provides students with a broad foundation in the discipline and the opportunity to specialize in one of several areas: physical geography, human geography, people–environment geography, or cartography and GIS. Students in the major develop skills in critical thinking, spatial analysis, and communication that prepare them for a wide range of careers in government, business, and non-profit organizations.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/geography-bs/geography-bs_requirementstext.pdf

Concentration name: Geology, Geophysics, Environmental Geology, General Geology
description: Geology and geophysics is the study of the Earth, including its composition, structure, physical properties, and history. Because the geosciences are a synthesis of other sciences, students in geology and geophysics also study mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. Geoscientists explore for natural resources (such as minerals, oil, and gas), manage water resources, and solve environmental problems. They also study natural hazards such as earthquakes, volcanoes, and landslides. The program in geology and geophysics provides students with a solid foundation in the geosciences and prepares them for a variety of careers in industry, government, and education, as well as for graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Geology and Geophysics
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Geoscience is a multi-disciplinary field that studies the features, processes and history of the earth, other planets, and their moons. Geoscience involves the study of the solid earth and its atmosphere, oceans, and biosphere. By understanding the earth’s history, geoscientists are better able to predict future changes in the environment. Many geoscientists work to solve problems related to earth resources, environmental protection, and natural hazards such as earthquakes, floods, and landslides.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Geology and Geophysics
Program Page url: https://partner.studymetro.com/s/course-session/a0C2x00000POxGKEA1/pn399473

description: German is the native language of some 100 million people. It is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union, and one of the world's most important languages of commerce and technology. German culture has for centuries been at the core of the humanities in the West. It is the language of Goethe, Kafka, and Brecht; of Luther, Freud, and Marx; of Mozart, Beethoven, and Wagner; and of Kant, Nietzsche, and Heidegger. UW–Madison's German program is one of the largest and strongest in the United States. Its curriculum is designed to lead students to a high level of proficiency in the language and to provide them with a deep understanding of the cultures of the German-speaking world. Students in the program explore a full range of topics, including literature and philosophy, linguistics, history and politics, film and popular culture, and more. Most of our students take advantage of the opportunity to study in Germany on one of our several study abroad programs.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: German is the official language of Germany, Austria, and Liechtenstein, and it is one of the official languages of Switzerland and Luxembourg. It is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union and is one of the world's most important languages of business, science, and technology. The German program offers students the opportunity to learn about the language, literature, and culture of German-speaking countries. One of the largest and most consistently top-ranked programs in the United States, the German program has a world-class faculty with expertise in areas ranging from linguistics to literature to culture. Our students study German for many different reasons: to travel and live in German-speaking countries; to learn more about their own heritage; to prepare for graduate study in German or other fields; or to broaden their intellectual horizons and develop their communicative skills.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The undergraduate certificate in Global Health provides students with a holistic framework for understanding the factors that influence health and disease at the local, national, and international levels. Through a combination of core courses, electives, and a global health-related field experience, students examine the biological, social, cultural, and environmental determinants of health and explore the impact of globalization on health outcomes. The certificate is intended to complement a student’s major and provide them with the knowledge and skills needed to address complex health challenges in an increasingly interconnected world.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Global Health
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/entomology/global-health-certificate/

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Health Promotion and Health Equity (HPHE) program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in health promotion, health equity, or a health-related field. This includes careers such as a community health specialist, public health educator, health researcher, or health policy analyst, or pursuing graduate work in medicine, physical therapy, occupational therapy, nursing, or public health. Students in the Health Promotion and Health Equity (HPHE) program develop skills to support people across the lifespan in various settings (e.g., community, workplace, school, clinical) to live their healthiest lives. These skills include learning how to assess the health needs of a community or population, create and implement health programs, and evaluate the effectiveness of these programs. The HPHE major is a collaborative program among three departments in the School of Education: Counseling Psychology, Kinesiology, and Rehabilitation Psychology and Special Education. The program is designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in health promotion and health equity by offering courses in these three departments.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Health Promotion and Health Equity
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/kinesiology/health-promotion-health-equity-bs/

description: History is more than just a list of names and dates; it’s the study of the past in all its complexity. From the origins of the world’s religions to the history of video games, our courses cover it all. At UW–Madison, students learn to explore how our world has changed and how it remains the same. History students engage with people and ideas from around the world and from every era. They also learn how to use evidence to build powerful arguments, think critically, and communicate effectively. For our graduates, history is a launchpad to a successful career. Our alumni work in every field imaginable, from medicine and law to business and the non-profit sector. Because of their unique combination of skills—research, communication, and critical thinking—history majors are always in demand.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/history/history-ba/history-ba.pdf

description: The study of history is a process of constant investigation. Historians use evidence from the past to understand the world we live in today. They study every imaginable aspect of human experience: politics and government, war and revolution, religion and culture, social life and the economy. History is a bridge between the humanities and the social sciences. It is also an incredibly flexible major that can be tailored to meet a student’s interests and goals. History majors learn to think critically, to write and speak with clarity and precision, to understand the diversity of human experience across time and space, and to evaluate various types of historical evidence. These skills are essential in any career.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/history/history-bs/history-bs_wisconsinexperiencetext.pdf

Concentration name: Organic and Sustainable Agriculture; Plant Science; Food and Ornamental Horticulture; Horticulture and Business
description: Horticulture is the science, art, and business of growing and using fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants. The horticulture major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills for careers in several areas including plant science, nursery and greenhouse management, landscape design, turfgrass management, and fruit and vegetable production. Students in the horticulture major can choose from several tracks: Organic and Sustainable Agriculture; Plant Science; Food and Ornamental Horticulture; or Horticulture and Business. Each track provides a solid foundation in basic sciences and plant biology while allowing students to focus on their specific interests. Horticulturalists use their knowledge to: breed and develop new plant varieties with improved traits like disease resistance, drought tolerance, and better flavor; develop sustainable production systems for fruits and vegetables; design and manage beautiful and functional gardens, parks, and landscapes; improve the quality of the environment by using plants to clean the air and water, and to reduce soil erosion; provide fresh, healthy food for people around the world; manage turfgrass for use in golf courses, athletic fields, and home lawns. In addition to being a science and an art, horticulture is also a business. Many horticulture graduates go on to own or manage their own businesses, such as greenhouses, nurseries, and landscape companies. Others work in sales, marketing, and management for large horticulture corporations. UW–Madison horticulture graduates are in high demand by employers. The department has a long history of excellence in research, teaching, and outreach, and its graduates are well-prepared for successful careers in the horticulture industry.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/plant-agroecosystem-sciences/horticulture-bs/

description: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) major focuses on the study of people and families. It is an interdisciplinary program that examines the psychological, social, and biological aspects of human development across the lifespan, and the ways in which families and other social contexts influence that development. Students in the HDFS major gain a deep understanding of how individuals and families grow, change, and interact with one another and their communities. They also learn how to apply this knowledge to improve the lives of individuals and families through research, policy, and practice. The HDFS major is an excellent choice for students who are interested in careers in human services, education, health care, law, or public policy. It also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in a variety of fields, including psychology, sociology, social work, and human development and family studies.
Accreditation status: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) major curriculum has been approved by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for the Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Studies
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The individual major provides a student with the opportunity to design a major when their academic interests are not fully met by any of the existing majors at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. This program is intended for students who have a focused area of study that is interdisciplinary in nature and cannot be met by an existing major or combination of majors and certificates. To be eligible for the individual major, a student must have a minimum of a 3.000 cumulative grade point average (GPA) on at least 30 credits in residence at UW–Madison. In addition, the student must have at least 30 degree credits remaining to be completed at the time the individual major is approved by the College of Letters & Science. The degree awarded is either a Bachelor of Arts (BA) or a Bachelor of Science (BS) in the Individual Major.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Individual Major
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Individual Major is an option for students who wish to pursue a program of study that is not available through an established major. Each student works with a faculty committee to design a major that is built around a coherent theme. The individual major must be significantly different from any existing major and must be interdisciplinary in nature. The major must be approved by the College of Letters & Science Faculty Committee on Individual Majors.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Individual Major
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Industrial engineers (IEs) are the only engineers trained to be specialists in productivity and quality improvement. IEs are people-oriented, and they enjoy the challenge of solving problems in many different environments. In addition to traditional manufacturing, industrial engineers work in such areas as healthcare, transportation, banking, insurance, and communication. Industrial engineers examine how to best use the resources available to provide a service or manufacture a product. This may involve the study of people, equipment, materials, and information. The industrial engineer makes sure that people have the best tools, workstation, and work environment to do their job. IEs also design the flow of work and the interaction of people and machines. Students study such things as time and motion, engineering management, work-system design, information systems, human factors, and ergonomics. Industrial engineering at UW–Madison is one of the top programs in the nation.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Businesses rely on information systems to function and compete in today’s economy. The Information Systems (IS) major prepares students for positions as IS professionals or for work in other functional areas where an understanding of information systems is essential. The IS major provides students with the technical, interpersonal, and business skills required to succeed in a variety of business-technology roles. Students explore how IS can provide value by improving business processes and providing better information for decision-making. Information systems are designed to help organizations reach their goals, and IS professionals design and implement these systems.
Program name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Information Systems
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/accounting-information-systems/

description: Interior architecture is a professional program that explores the relationship between human behavior and the environment. Designers find creative solutions for the spaces in which people live and work. They strive to improve the health, safety, and welfare of the public and to enhance the quality of life. The professional curriculum includes courses in hand drawing, CAD, 3D modeling, lighting, materials, color, building systems, and sustainable design. Professional practice, design for a variety of users, and space planning are also taught. Interior Architecture students work closely with design professors in a studio setting.
Accreditation status: The Interior Architecture program is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Interior Architecture
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: International business is a second major that provides students with the opportunity to gain a broader global perspective. Students will learn the significance of various global issues such as world trade, international management, and global marketing. The program’s mission is to offer a comprehensive, multidisciplinary curriculum that will help students think globally and prepare them for a variety of international careers. The international business major must be taken in conjunction with another business major. Students may not double major in international business and business: health care management.
Program name: Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/

Concentration name: Global Economy, Global Security, Culture in the Age of Globalization
description: The International Studies Major (IS Major) is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the world’s most pressing problems from a variety of perspectives. Students take courses in the social sciences, humanities, and professional schools to gain a broad understanding of international issues and then specialize in one of three thematic options: Global Economy, Global Security, or Culture in the Age of Globalization. The IS Major provides students with the tools to understand the complex interactions between states, non-state actors, and individuals in the global arena.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/international-studies-bs/international-studies-bs.pdf

Concentration name: Global Security, Global Economy, or Culture in the Age of Globalization
description: International Studies (IS) is a multidisciplinary major that allows students to explore how global processes—be they economic, political, or cultural—interact with each other and with specific places around the world. The major is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous foundation for understanding the complex issues that characterize our modern world. In addition to a core set of courses in international studies, students choose a track (option) in one of three areas: Global Security, Global Economy, or Culture in the Age of Globalization. Students also take courses that focus on a specific region of the world (e.g., Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, Middle East, Russia/Central Eurasia). To gain further depth, students must complete at least five semesters of a single foreign language. As a result of this training, IS majors are prepared for a range of careers in both the public and private sectors, including government, international organizations, business, and non-profit organizations.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in International Studies
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/international-studies-bs/

description: Italian at UW–Madison is a vibrant, well-rounded program that offers students a great deal of flexibility. Students who major in Italian will gain a high level of language proficiency and an in-depth understanding of Italian culture. We offer courses on topics as diverse as Italian cuisine, cinema, comics and graphic novels, the Renaissance, and opera. Our students also study the work of many major figures of Italian literature such as Dante, Machiavelli, and Elena Ferrante. Students can take most of these courses in Italian or in English. Students may choose to focus more on language and culture or on literature. To gain even more proficiency, many Italian majors spend a summer, a semester, or a year studying in Italy through one of the university’s many study abroad programs. Students who study Italian find that their language and culture skills make them strong candidates for a variety of careers in fields such as business, law, fashion, the food and beverage industry, design, education, and international relations.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/french-italian/italian-ba/

description: The Department of French and Italian offers students a wealth of opportunities for the study of the languages and cultures of France, Italy, and other countries where French or Italian is spoken. Our students explore the literature and culture of these countries from the Middle Ages to the present day. Students can also study Italian and French for business and take courses in cinema and media studies, gender and women's studies, second language acquisition, and food studies. In all of our programs, students develop communicative and cultural competency as well as strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Our majors find careers in a wide range of fields including business, law, international relations, education, journalism, non-profit management, and public policy.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Japanese is one of the world's major languages. In addition to being spoken by the 127 million people who live in Japan, it is also used as a second language by people in Chinese and Korean communities and other parts of Asia. Knowledge of Japanese is becoming more and more important as Japan's role as a major economic power and its importance in international politics increases. The undergraduate major in Japanese is designed to provide students with proficiency in the Japanese language and a solid foundation in Japanese literature and culture. It is intended both for students who wish to pursue a career in such fields as business, government, or journalism, and for those who intend to go on to graduate study in Japanese literature or linguistics.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Department of Asian Languages and Cultures (ALC) offers a wide range of courses on the languages, literatures, and cultures of East, South, and Southeast Asia. ALC's undergraduate programs are designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in the traditions and contemporary developments of these regions. The department offers three undergraduate majors: Chinese, Japanese, and Languages and Cultures of Asia. The Japanese major provides students with a high level of proficiency in Japanese language and a deep understanding of Japanese culture, literature, and history. Students in the Japanese major develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural communication, and linguistic analysis.

The program focuses on the biological and behavioral aspects of movement. Students take a core of foundation courses, including anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor learning and control, and the psychology and sociology of physical activity. This broad foundation prepares students for a wide range of careers in health and fitness, as well as for further study in graduate or professional programs, such as physical therapy, occupational therapy, medicine, and other health-related fields.

The program focuses on the design, planning, and management of the land to create sustainable and resilient communities and environments. Students in the BLA program learn how to analyze, design, and manage natural and built environments through a curriculum that integrates design studio, ecology, technology, and professional practice.

It is a profession that combines art and science to create places for people while protecting and restoring the environment. Landscape architects work on a wide variety of projects, from small urban gardens to large-scale regional plans. Students take a sequence of studio courses that develop the design, technical, and communication skills of the landscape architect. Students in the BSLA program learn to use a variety of tools and techniques to design and communicate their ideas. They also learn about the history and theory of landscape architecture, as well as the environmental and social factors that influence the design process. description: The Latin major is designed to provide students with a high level of proficiency in the Latin language, a good knowledge of the literature, and a broad understanding of the Roman world. Students who complete the major will have a solid understanding of the Latin language and its literature, and will be able to read and analyze a wide variety of texts. The major also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in classics, archaeology, ancient history, and other related fields. Students learn to: apply the concepts of grammar, syntax, and morphology to the translation of Latin texts; analyze the formal and thematic features of Latin literature in its historical and cultural context; evaluate the reception and influence of Latin literature and Roman culture on subsequent periods and cultures; and produce clear and effective writing and research on topics related to Latin literature and Roman culture.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The department offers two undergraduate majors: Latin and Classics. Students who choose the Latin major study the language, literature, and culture of the Roman world. Latin is the language of the Roman Empire and the common language of intellectual, legal, and religious life in Europe through the Middle Ages and into the early modern period. Students who major in Latin gain a deep understanding of the language, literature, and history of Rome and its influence on later cultures. Latin students develop strong analytical and communication skills that are valuable for careers in many fields, including education, law, medicine, and business. Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: Latin American, Caribbean, and Iberian Studies (LACIS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers an undergraduate major and a certificate. LACIS majors and certificate students are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Latin America, the Caribbean, Spain, or Portugal, and to seek out internships that allow them to apply their knowledge in a professional setting. description: The Legal Studies major is designed to provide a liberal arts education for students who wish to study law and its relationship to society, and who may or may not be considering a career in the legal profession. As an interdisciplinary major, Legal Studies is composed of several themes: legal institutions; law and social forces; law and culture; and law and theory. The program focuses on law and its relationship to society, rather than on the practice of law.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies

description: Legal studies is an interdisciplinary major that provides an opportunity for students to study law and legal institutions in their social, economic, and political contexts. The program is designed to provide students with a broad education in the liberal arts and sciences. It is not a professional program or a pre-law program. The major is designed to help students understand how law works in society and how society works in law. The curriculum is organized around five themes: legal institutions; processes of legal order and disorder; law and social forces; law and culture; and law and theory. The major is housed in the Center for Law, Society & Justice. Legal studies is a well-established discipline within the liberal arts. Many of the most important thinkers in the development of Western and non-Western thought have grappled with the role of law in society. The legal studies major offers students the opportunity to learn from faculty members from across the campus who bring their own disciplinary perspectives to the study of law. The program also offers a wide range of internship and other learning opportunities beyond the classroom.

description: Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. It seeks to discover the principles that underlie the structure and use of all languages. Linguists investigate a wide range of questions: How do the sounds of a language relate to its meanings? How does language change over time? What is the relationship between language and the brain? How does language vary from one social group to another? What are the commonalities between all languages? What can language tell us about human nature? Students who major in linguistics learn how to analyze the structure of language, how language is used in social contexts, and how language is processed in the brain. They also develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills that are valuable in a variety of careers.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/language-sciences/linguistics-bs/linguistics-bs.pdf

description: Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. It is a wide-ranging field that includes the study of language structure (grammar), language meaning (semantics and pragmatics), language sounds (phonetics and phonology), and how these things change over time. It also includes the study of how people learn languages (language acquisition), how language is used in social contexts (sociolinguistics), and how it is processed in the brain (psycholinguistics and neurolinguistics). Linguists are interested in identifying the properties that all languages share and the ways in which they differ. They also want to understand the nature of the human capacity for language and how it interacts with other aspects of cognition. The undergraduate major in linguistics at UW–Madison provides a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistic analysis, as well as the opportunity to explore more specialized areas of the field. Students learn to analyze language data from a wide variety of languages and to think critically about the nature of language and its role in human life.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The management and human resources major offers two distinct options: Human Resources or Management. The human resources option focuses on the people side of business, including staff recruitment and selection, performance management, employee relations, diversity and inclusion, and compensation and benefits. The management option focuses on the broader set of leadership and managerial skills needed to be successful in any organization. Students learn about organizational behavior, leadership, strategy, entrepreneurship, and innovation. The management and human resources major provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to be effective leaders and managers in a variety of organizational settings.
Program name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management and Human Resources

description: Materials science and engineering (MS&E) is a field that involves the discovery and design of new materials, with a focus on solids. Materials scientists and engineers study the relationships between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Based on this understanding, they design and manufacture materials to meet specific requirements for applications in various fields such as electronics, energy, healthcare, and transportation. The materials science and engineering program at UW–Madison is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the physical and engineering sciences. The curriculum emphasizes the fundamental principles of thermodynamics, kinetics, and structure-property relationships, while also providing hands-on experience in materials characterization and processing. This foundation is designed to prepare students for a wide range of career opportunities in industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and healthcare, as well as for further study in graduate school.

The Department of Mathematics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a world leader in mathematical research and education. Our faculty and students are involved in research that spans the entire range of mathematics, from the most abstract theoretical work to the most applied projects. A student who majors in mathematics will find that it is a discipline that is both challenging and rewarding. The mathematics major provides a solid foundation for students who are interested in pursuing a career in a wide range of fields, including finance, technology, education, and research. description: Mathematics is a multifaceted subject of great beauty and application. The mathematics major at UW–Madison is a flexible program that can be tailored to meet a student’s particular interests. description: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms—bacteria, viruses, fungi, algae, and protozoa. These tiny life forms are critical to our world. They are the basis of the food chain, they support the life of plants and animals, and they help recycle the world's resources. Some are also the cause of major diseases, such as AIDS, tuberculosis, and many others. Microbiology is an exciting field that contributes to the areas of medicine, genetics, molecular biology, pharmacy, agriculture, and environmental science. A microbiology major prepares students for many different careers in health care, industry, research, and government. It also provides an excellent background for medical, dental, or veterinary school, and for graduate study in any of the biological sciences. The Microbiology major is offered by the Department of Bacteriology in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences. The Department of Medical Microbiology and Immunology in the School of Medicine and Public Health also participates in the program.

description: Molecular biology is the study of the molecular basis of life. It is a rapidly growing field that has revolutionized our understanding of biology and medicine. The molecular biology major is an interdisciplinary program that draws on the expertise of faculty from across the university. The major is designed to provide students with a rigorous and broad-based education in the biological sciences, with a focus on the molecular and cellular levels. Students in the major will learn about the structure and function of biological molecules, the mechanisms of gene expression and regulation, and the molecular basis of disease. The major also provides students with the opportunity to gain research experience through independent study and honors research projects. The molecular biology major is an excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue careers in research, medicine, or biotechnology.

The MCB major provides students with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of molecular and cell biology, as well as opportunities to explore specialized areas such as developmental biology, neurobiology, and immunology. Students in the MCB major will develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills through coursework and laboratory research. description: Neurobiology is the study of the nervous system, which includes the brain, spinal cord, and individual nerve cells. The major serves as excellent preparation for students interested in pursuing advanced degrees in medicine, veterinary medicine, physical therapy, and other healthcare professions, as well as graduate studies in neurobiology, psychology, and related fields.

description: Neurobiology is the study of the nervous system: how it is built, how it works, and how it changes. Toxicology is the study of the adverse effects of drugs and other chemicals on living systems. It involves understanding how chemicals can cause harm, how they can be detected and measured, and how their effects can be prevented or treated. The Bachelor of Science in Pharmacology and Toxicology program is an undergraduate major within the School of Pharmacy. This program provides a unique opportunity for students to study the biomedical sciences and their application to drug discovery and development. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and math) followed by advanced coursework in pharmacology and toxicology. The program’s core courses include human physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, and toxicology. Students also choose from a wide range of elective courses in areas such as immunology, neuroscience, and public health. In addition to coursework, students have the opportunity to participate in research with faculty in the School of Pharmacy and other departments across campus. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, government agencies, and academia. They are also well-qualified for further graduate or professional study in fields such as medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and the biomedical sciences.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Pharmacology and Toxicology

description: The Department of Philosophy offers an undergraduate major leading to the bachelor of arts or the bachelor of science degree. Philosophy is the study of fundamental questions about the nature of reality, knowledge, and value. The department's courses are designed to provide students with a broad education in these areas, and to develop their abilities to think critically, write clearly, and reason logically. Philosophy is an excellent major for students who are interested in law, medicine, business, or any other field that requires the ability to analyze complex arguments and to communicate effectively.

description: Philosophy is the study of the most fundamental questions that arise in reflecting on the nature of the world and the place of human beings in it. What is the nature of reality? What can we know? What is the basis of our moral beliefs? What are the characteristics of a just society? What is the relationship between the mind and the body? description: Landscape architecture is a profession that covers a wide range of activities. At its most fundamental level, landscape architecture is the design of the land. Its focus is on the creation of more enjoyable, comfortable, and sustainable outdoor environments. Landscape architects may find themselves working on a wide range of project types, from residential gardens to city parks and riverfronts, from corporate office parks to new communities, and from garden restoration to ecological heritage. The certificate in landscape architecture is available for any student who has an interest in the field of landscape architecture and its environmental, social, and aesthetic applications. This program provides students with an introduction to the history of the field and its design and planning processes.

description: The University of Wisconsin–Madison Leadership Certificate is a program designed to recognize students' leadership development both in and out of the classroom. The program's purpose is to: 1. Acknowledge and recognize student leadership excellence at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. 2. Support the development of student leadership throughout the University of Wisconsin-Madison. 3. Assist in the process of translating leadership experiences into future professional and academic endeavors. 4. Encourage students to create a leadership 'identity' through the use of the UW-Madison Leadership Framework. The UW-Madison Leadership Certificate is open to all UW–Madison undergraduate and graduate/professional students.

description: The LGBTQ+ studies certificate is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with an opportunity to examine the history, culture, and social experiences of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer people. Students will explore how sexual and gender identities intersect with other social categories, such as race, ethnicity, class, and disability. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills to work effectively with diverse populations and to prepare them for careers in a variety of fields, including social services, health care, education, and law.

description: Material culture is the study of objects—from those of the everyday to the extraordinary—and the way they shape and are shaped by the people who make and use them. Our relationship to the material world is at the core of human history, and we believe that to study things is to better understand ourselves. The Material Culture Program is a collaborative, interdisciplinary community of students and faculty members across the UW–Madison campus who use material things as primary sources for research and as powerful tools for teaching. Our interdisciplinary reach spans numerous departments, representing such diverse fields as Art History, Design Studies, Anthropology, Folklore, Landscape Architecture, Geography, and History. The Certificate in Material Culture program offers students an opportunity to learn how to research and interpret the material world, and provides them with a set of skills that can be applied to many different fields. Students learn about the various ways in which material culture has been studied in the past and how it is being studied today. They also gain hands-on experience in the research, documentation, and interpretation of material objects.

description: The Mathematics certificate allows students to pursue their interest in mathematics while completing a major in another field. The certificate is intended to provide a broad introduction to some of the most important ideas in mathematics, as well as to develop the student's ability to think critically and solve problems. The certificate can be a valuable addition to a variety of majors, as mathematical skills are increasingly in demand in many fields.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Medieval Studies Certificate allows students to explore the Middle Ages as an interdisciplinary phenomenon. This fascinating era (roughly 500-1500 CE) saw the formation of Europe, the development of modern European languages, the growth of the Christian church, and the rise of Islam. Medieval culture and history are important to any student interested in the origins of Western civilization. Medieval studies also includes the study of the Byzantine Empire and the Islamic world, as well as the relationships between the Latin West and these other cultures. The certificate is designed for students who want to explore this period from a variety of perspectives, using the resources of several departments. It is an excellent complement to many majors, providing a focus for students' elective courses.
Program Page url: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

description: The Certificate in Middle East Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who wish to explore the history, culture, and politics of the Middle East while pursuing a degree in another field. The certificate is administered by the Institute for Regional and International Studies (IRIS). Students choose from a wide variety of courses in departments across the university, including African Cultural Studies, Anthropology, Art History, Classics, Economics, Geography, History, Languages and Cultures of Asia, Political Science, Religious Studies, and Sociology. Completion of the Middle East Studies Certificate will be noted on a student's transcript.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/middle-east-studies-certificate/

description: The Certificate in Music is intended for students who wish to pursue a course of study in music while completing a degree in another field. The certificate offers two options for study: performance and non-performance. The non-performance option is open to all students and does not require an audition. The performance-based option requires an audition and provides the opportunity for students to receive high-level individual performance instruction while participating in School of Music ensembles and taking music theory and history courses. Students may find it difficult to complete the certificate in Music Performance within four years, as it requires four semesters of individual performance instruction and three additional semesters of music theory and history. To avoid this, students are encouraged to audition and begin taking the required music theory and history courses as early as possible.

description: The PEPP certificate is designed to provide students with the opportunity to study the intersection of politics, economics and philosophy. The core of the certificate is a three-course sequence (one in each field) that introduces students to the different ways in which these disciplines approach questions of justice, efficiency and governance. In addition to the core courses, students take three elective courses that allow them to explore specific topics in more depth.
Program Page url: https://polisci.wisc.edu/2017/05/15/pepp-certificate/

description: The Certificate in Political Economy, Philosophy, and Politics (PEPP) is designed for students who want to study the intersection of these three disciplines. The program is based on the idea that each of these fields provides a different perspective on the world and that understanding the world requires an appreciation of all three. Political economy studies how people organize themselves to produce and distribute goods and services. Philosophy explores the fundamental questions of human existence, such as the nature of justice, the role of government, and the meaning of life. Politics is the study of how people make decisions together and how power is exercised in society. By studying these three fields together, students will gain a deeper understanding of the complex challenges facing the world today and the different ways that people are trying to address them. The PEPP certificate is open to all students at UW-Madison and is particularly well-suited for students who are interested in pursuing careers in law, public policy, business, or international affairs.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/political-science/political-economy-philosophy-politics-certificate/

description: The Promoting Activity for Diverse Abilities (PADA) certificate is for undergraduate students who want to develop the knowledge and skills to provide physical activity programming for individuals with disabilities. Students will complete foundational and applied coursework in physical activity for individuals with disabilities, and will apply their knowledge in a community-based practicum experience. This certificate will enhance the professional preparation of students pursuing careers in education, healthcare (e.g., physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant), and physical activity (e.g., fitness and wellness, personal training).
Program name: Certificate in Promoting Activity for Diverse Abilities
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/kinesiology/promoting-activity-diverse-abilities-certificate/

description: The Certificate in Education and Educational Services (CEES) provides students with a cohesive set of courses focusing on the study and practice of education. The certificate is designed for students who are interested in the many facets of education but do not necessarily wish to complete a teacher certification program. The certificate is intended to help students: 1. understand the importance of education in today’s world; 2. understand the complexities of the educational process; 3. understand the myriad of ways in which one can work in education and educational service-related fields; 4. prepare for a variety of education-related careers; and 5. obtain an understanding of the relationship between education and their major area of study.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/educational-psychology/education-educational-services-certificate/

description: The undergraduate Certificate in Public Policy allows students to apply the skills they learn in their majors to real-world issues. It is intended for students who wish to better understand how public policy is made and the role that economics, politics, and power play in the policy-making process. Students will develop skills in policy analysis and learn how to write for a policy audience. They will also learn how to apply these skills to a range of substantive policy areas such as health, the environment, social welfare, or technology.

description: Religious studies is an interdisciplinary program that offers students the opportunity to explore the diverse phenomena of religion around the world from a variety of perspectives. Our faculty come from many departments across the university, and our courses cover a wide range of religious traditions, including Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, and Judaism, as well as indigenous and new religious movements. We offer a major and a certificate, both of which are designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the role of religion in human life, as well as the opportunity to focus on specific traditions or themes.

description: The Certificate in Russian, East European, and Central Asian Studies (REECAS) is designed to give students a multidisciplinary survey of the region. The REECAS region is a vast and diverse area of the world that includes Russia, Eastern and Central Europe, and the Caucasus and Central Asia. The certificate is open to all undergraduates and provides students with the opportunity to explore the history, politics, culture, and languages of this region.
Program name: Certificate in Russian, East European and Central Asian Studies

description: The Department of German, Nordic, and Slavic+ offers several options for the study of Scandinavian (Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian, and Swedish) language, literature, and culture. Courses in Scandinavian provide a window into the culture and history of the Nordic countries, and also serve as a tool for understanding the rich and diverse heritage of many people in the Upper Midwest. Many students find that Scandinavian studies is a great addition to their primary major. For example, a student majoring in nursing might want to learn more about the healthcare systems in Scandinavia. A student majoring in political science or international studies may be interested in learning about the Nordic model of social welfare. A student majoring in art history might find inspiration in the work of Edvard Munch or the design of IKEA. No matter what your interests are, the Scandinavian Studies certificate can help you develop a deeper understanding of the world.

description: The Graduate/Professional Certificate in the Science of Patient Safety program is designed for graduate students in the health sciences and engineering and for healthcare professionals. The certificate provides students with the knowledge and skills to apply the concepts and methods of the science of patient safety to their own practice or research. The science of patient safety is an interdisciplinary field that draws on the theories and methods of human factors engineering, health services research, and health care quality improvement. The certificate program is a joint effort of the Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISyE) in the College of Engineering and several health sciences schools (Medicine and Public Health, Nursing, and Pharmacy).
Program name: Certificate in Science of Patient Safety

description: The undergraduate Certificate in South Asian Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the diversity and complexity of the South Asian region. South Asia includes the countries of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Students can choose from a range of courses in departments across the university. They explore themes such as religion and philosophy; the arts and literature; history; politics, society, and economics; and the environment. This certificate can be a valuable addition to any major, providing students with a deeper understanding of one of the world's most populous and influential regions.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/south-asian-studies-certificate/

description: Southeast Asia is a region of diversity, encompassing the nations of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar (Burma), the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam. The Certificate in Southeast Asian Studies is designed to provide students with a multidisciplinary grounding in the languages, histories, and cultures of Southeast Asia. It is an excellent way to organize a set of courses around a regional interest, and to have that interest recognized on one’s transcript. The certificate is open to all undergraduate students and is particularly relevant to those planning careers in international business, government, non-governmental organizations, or education. Southeast Asian Studies is a program of the Center for Southeast Asian Studies. The center also offers a major in Southeast Asian Studies through the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures. The Center for Southeast Asian Studies is a Title VI National Resource Center.
Program Page url: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/southeast-asian-studies-certificate/

Our Spanish program offers a wealth of courses in the areas of language, literature, culture, and linguistics. This certificate program is for students who want to develop their proficiency in Spanish, as well as their knowledge of the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

description: The Sustainability Certificate is for undergraduate students who wish to learn about the environmental, social and economic dimensions of sustainability. This is accomplished through a combination of coursework and a capstone project. The certificate is designed to be flexible and can be completed by students from any major. The certificate is a collaborative effort between the Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Office of Sustainability.

description: The Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) provides an opportunity for undergraduate students at UW–Madison to develop a basic foundation in linguistics and second language acquisition, to investigate the history and politics of English language teaching, and to explore and apply various methods for teaching English to adult learners in the U.S. and abroad. TESOL certificate students will understand how English is structured and used in various contexts, learn how to design and evaluate instructional materials, and observe and practice teaching English in local contexts. The certificate is open to undergraduate students in any major, and it is a popular credential for students planning to live and work abroad after graduation. The TESOL certificate is not a program that leads to Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction (DPI) teacher certification for K–12 schools.
Program name: Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages

This certificate allows students to acquire a collection of courses that focuses on the textile and fashion industry as a creative and/or commercial entity. Students choose between a design or business focus.

description: The certificate in theatre provides students with a broad introduction to the field of theatre and drama and the opportunity to complete work in several areas: acting, stage management, scenic design, costume design, lighting design, theatre technology, and/or theatre history and literature. The certificate can also be used as a way to focus on a specific area of interest. Any undergraduate student may declare the theatre certificate. Most certificate students also choose to participate in university theatre productions in a variety of ways: acting, backstage crew, house management, or design.

description: The Certificate in Visual Culture provides an opportunity for students to pursue a sustained and focused interest in the history and theory of images and the visual world. It is designed to allow students to choose a set of courses that suits their individual interests and goals from the many visual culture courses offered across the campus. Students are introduced to the fundamental concepts and methods of visual culture through a required core course and develop those interests in greater depth through a 400-level seminar or other advanced course. At the same time, the certificate allows for a maximum of flexibility. Students are encouraged to explore the intersections between visual culture and their primary major, and to build on their own particular interests by choosing from a wide variety of electives. The Certificate in Visual Culture is an interdisciplinary program open to any undergraduate student at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
